summary: Dörte Kamarid is a scholar in Tibetology and Indology. She studied at the University of Vienna, Savitribai Phule Pune University, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, completing an MA under the supervision of Helmut Tauscher.

E. Adelaide Hahn was a linguist who studied at Hunter College and Columbia University under Edgar Howard Sturtevant, Leonard Bloomfield, and Franklin Edgerton. She served at Hunter College (1915–1963) and was President of the Linguistic Society of America in 1946.

E. Baer was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. Baer studied at the University of Basel and the University of Zurich, earning a PhD and studying under Adolf Kaegi, Jakob Hausheer, Eduard Schwyzer, and Emil Abegg.
E. Easwaran Nampoothiry is an Indologist who studied under S. Venkitasubramonia Iyer. He served as a lecturer in the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Kerala (attested 1973).

E. F. Schumacher was a philosopher who studied at the University of Bonn, New College, Columbia University, and the London School of Economics, also studying under Edward Conze. He held posts at Columbia University (~1934–1935) and the University of Oxford (~1942–1944).

E. Gene Smith was a Tibetologist who studied at institutions including the University of Washington under Turrell V. Wylie and with traditional Tibetan teachers. He worked for the Library of Congress and founded and directed the Buddhist Digital Resource Center (1999–2010).
E. H. Hall worked in Indology and linguistics. Hall studied under George Abraham Grierson and served as a clerk at the India Office Records.
E. H. Rogers was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He served as Head Master at The Lawrence School, Sanawar, in 1858 and as a Sub-Inspector for Army Schools in 1861.
E. M. Hare was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He was educated at Stamford School and studied as a pupil under Frank Lee Woodward.

E. Michael Mendelson worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at King's College, Cambridge, the University of Chicago (~1949–1951), and the University of Paris (~1951–1956), and taught Jane Bunnag.

E. R. Sreekrishna Sarma was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Marburg (~1951–1954) under Johannes Nobel, and later held a post at Sri Venkateswara University (~1961–1982).

E. Sherman Oakley was an Indologist who studied at the University of Glasgow, Airedale Independent College, and the University of Allahabad. He served with the London Missionary Society from 1888 and was Principal of Ramsay College.

E. W. Adikaram was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Colombo, SOAS, and the University of London under William Stede. In 1934, he became principal of Ananda Sastralaya, Kotte.

Ebbe Oskar Tuneld was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Lund University, Berlin, Leipzig, Göttingen under Hermann Oldenberg, and Paris under Antoine Meillet and Sylvain Lévi. He served as PD and Professor of Indology at Lund University (from 1915).

Ebenezer Burgess studied at Amherst College (~1827–1831) and Andover Theological Seminary (~1834–1837). He served as a missionary for the American Board of Commissioners for Foreign Missions from 1839 to 1854.

Ebenezer Charles Bethlehem Hallam was an Indologist and linguist educated at King Edward's School, Birmingham, and Toronto Normal School. He served as a missionary with the American Free Baptist Mission (1857–1872) and the Baptist Missionary Society (~1856–1881).

Eberhard Fischer is an Indologist and historian who earned his PhD at the University of Basel (~1960–1965). He served as Director of Museum Rietberg (1972–1998) and Secretary General of the Swiss-Liechtenstein Foundation for Archaeological Research Abroad (~1998).

Eberhard Gothein was an economic historian who studied at Breslau and Heidelberg under Wilhelm Dilthey. He served as Professor of Nationalökonomie at Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (1884–1890), the University of Bonn (1890–1905), and Heidelberg University (from 1905).

Eberhard Sandschneider is a Sinologist who completed his education and PhD at Saarland University. He served as professor at Mainz (1995–1998), managing director at the Free University of Berlin (1999–2001), and Otto-Wolff-Direktor at the German Council on Foreign Relations (2003–2016).

Eberhard Schrader was a linguist who studied at the University of Göttingen under Heinrich Ewald. He held posts at the universities of Zurich, Giessen, and Jena before serving as Professor at the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1875–1908).
